text: We need a tool to train our whole workforce and prove it, from first enrollment to audit-ready completion records. Build my Learning Management System (LMS) module with Semantius.
Clean workspace confirmed — no training tables yet. I'll draft your LMS structure based on how leading platforms handle enrollments and completions, then verify the design.

Following TalentLMS, Docebo and Moodle — from my knowledge of the LMS category. They all agree on Courses, content Units, Enrollments, Assessments and Certificates, and that agreement is the outline below.

The mechanism your goal turns on is enrollment-to-proof: an Enrollment tracks a learner from assigned to completed, and a Certificate is issued as the audit-ready completion record. I deliberately keep grades/badges out — completion plus assessment pass covers proof without enterprise extras.

Confirm the entity list for your Learning Management System:

* Courses: training offerings the workforce must take; the catalog everything else hangs off
* Lessons: content steps inside a Course; each belongs to a Course
* Enrollments: a learner assigned to a Course; each belongs to a Course and names a learner in Users
* Assessments: checks that prove learning for a Course; each belongs to a Course
* Certificates: audit-ready proof of completion; each belongs to an Enrollment
* Users: existing, platform users; Enrollments name a learner, Courses name an instructor

How should I design the Learning Management System?

A. With all 5: Courses, Lessons, Enrollments, Assessments, Certificates (recommended).

B. With the core 4: Courses, Lessons, Enrollments, Certificates — Assessments as a follow-up.

Reply with A or B, or tell me what to add, drop or rename.
Verification needs one more clean run to confirm nothing changed.

text:
Built your Learning Management System: courses, lessons, enrollments with verification, assessments and certificates.

Open it here: https://tests.semantius.app/lms

**Access: gated.** Some steps are restricted to a role. Role names start with "Learning Management System".

| Role | Does | Sees |
|---|---|---|
| Viewer | reads only | everything |
| Manager | the everyday work | everything |
| Admin | the everyday work and every restricted step | everything |
| Learner | writes enrollments only | only the enrollments that name them, with their certificates; all other records |
| Instructor | writes lessons only | only the courses that name them, with their lessons, enrollments, assessments and certificates |
| Manager Approver | the everyday work; marks enrollments Verified | everything |

**Restricted steps**
- Enrollments → Verified: Manager Approver. An enrollment must be verified before it is completed or expired. When the enrollment names a manager approver, only that person or an admin. The requester may not approve it; only a submitted one is approved; what it covers is locked from submitted on; only the requester recalls it; only the approver rejects it or moves it back; who approved it and when is recorded.

**No restricted step** on Courses or Assessments: anyone who can edit one can move it through every state.

Assign people the Learner, Instructor and Manager Approver roles (role names: lms_learner, lms_instructor, lms_manager_approver).

Next steps: add your first course, import training records from CSV, assign roles to your team.

Should I add a small demo dataset so you can review the module, or leave the tables empty for your real data?

A. Sample data (recommended): 25 records across 5 tables (Courses, Lessons, Enrollments, Assessments, Certificates).

B. Empty tables: nothing is seeded.

Reply with A or B.
Demo data adjusted — importing and verifying.
